answer: Every fresh alias dilutes the cluster's average standing, so the larger the flock the weaker each individual vote becomes — coordination requires many low-weight votes that cancel each other out. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a grove as the anchor of the cost.
